title: The Hawk and the Pigeons
text:
A flock of pigeons lived in fear of a kite. Every so often it swooped on the dovecote and carried one of them off, and the pigeons could find no way to stop it.

At last they had an idea. The hawk was stronger than the kite and could drive it away. They went to the hawk and asked him to be their defender. He agreed at once, with every appearance of goodwill, and they opened the dovecote and invited him in.

The arrangement did keep the kite away. But once the hawk was inside, he began to feed on the pigeons himself, and he was far hungrier and far closer than the kite had ever been. In a single day, the fable says, he killed more of them than the kite had managed to take in a whole year. The pigeons had found their protector, and he was the worst thing that had ever happened to them.
lesson: When you are afraid, be careful whom you invite in to make the fear go away. Judge a protector by what he will do once he is inside, not by the danger he promises to remove.
people: The pigeons, a kite, a hawk
source: Aesop's Fables, The Hawk, the Kite, and the Pigeons
